# Introduction and Purpose

## Overview
The Political/Economic Discussion Board is designed as a vibrant digital space where registered members can participate in profound conversations about political and economic topics. By fostering respectful debate and information sharing, the platform aims to enhance understanding, civic engagement, and awareness among diverse user groups. The board provides tools for structured dialogue, content moderation, and policy enforcement—ensuring a safe, fair, and productive environment for all participants.

## Vision
Our vision is to become the most trusted, inclusive, and well-moderated online community for political and economic discussions. The platform strives to:
- Encourage diverse perspectives and in-depth analysis
- Facilitate respectful, evidence-based debates
- Protect members' freedom of expression within policy boundaries
- Minimize misinformation, abuse, and disruptive behavior

## Mission
- To provide an accessible and user-friendly forum allowing users to create, share, discuss, and report posts about political and economic issues
- To implement a reliable moderation system that efficiently addresses violations, ensuring constructive conversations
- To empower users with self-governing tools under the guidance of transparent policies

## Core Values
- **Inclusivity**: Embracing participants from diverse backgrounds and viewpoints
- **Integrity**: Upholding the highest standards of honesty and respect in discussions
- **Transparency**: Clear rules, visible moderation outcomes, and participatory governance
- **Security**: Safeguarding personal data, preventing manipulation and harassment

## Target Audience
- **General Members**: Internet users interested in political/economic topics, seeking a structured community to discuss ideas freely and safely
- **Moderators**: Trusted members committed to nurturing quality discourse and enforcing platform policies
- **Administrators**: Professionals responsible for platform integrity, continuous improvement, and high-level configuration

## Service Scope
- Multiple discussion threads and comment chains on political/economic topics
- User-driven content creation, editing, reporting, and feedback mechanisms
- An evolving moderation workflow to review, act, and resolve reported issues
- Administrative tools for policy management and platform oversight

## Document Structure and Next Steps
This introduction establishes the guiding principles and boundaries of the discussion board service. Subsequent documents will cover detailed user roles and journeys, platform requirements, workflow models, and policy outlines to support successful development and operation of the platform.

# Discussion Board User Roles and User Journeys

## Overview
This document defines the distinct user roles for the political/economic discussion board service and maps their corresponding permissions. It also describes the main user scenarios to ensure clarity regarding authentication, authorization, and access flows within the platform.

## 1. User Roles and Permissions

| Role      | Description                                                                                    | Permissions                                                                        |
|-----------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Member    | Registered user who participates in discussions and uses standard board features.              | - Create, read, edit, and delete own posts/comments  
- Report others' content  
- View and search board content                                                        |
| Moderator | Elevated privileges to enforce board policy, mediate disputes, and respond to reported issues. | - All Member permissions  
- Review and take action on reported items  
- Edit/remove any post/comment violating policies  
- Temporarily suspend or warn users                                                   |
| Admin     | System-level manager overseeing the platform's configuration and health.                      | - All Member and Moderator permissions  
- Manage user and moderator assignments  
- Configure global board settings  
- Oversee content moderation controls                                                  |

## 2. Core User Journeys

### 2.1 Member
- **Registration/Authentication**: Sign up and log into the platform with valid credentials.
- **Content Creation**: Compose and publish new discussion posts, edit or delete their own contributions.
- **Engagement**: Comment on posts, participate in threads, interact with other members within policy guidelines.
- **Reporting**: Identify and report posts or comments that violate board policies.
- **Profile Management**: Update profile information, view participation history.

### 2.2 Moderator
- **Content Review**: Access and manage flagged reports from members; review for policy violations.
- **Moderation Actions**: Edit, delete, or restore posts/comments as required; issue warnings or temporary suspensions to members.
- **Community Guidance**: Respond to disputes, clarifying rules and mediation between users.
- **Oversight**: Monitor board health by observing activity patterns, ensuring a respectful environment.

### 2.3 Admin
- **User and Role Management**: Assign or revoke moderator rights, manage user statuses (active, suspended, banned).
- **System Configuration**: Adjust board-level policies, privacy settings, and other administrative parameters.
- **Audit and Compliance**: Oversee all content and actions for compliance with board guidelines and broader legal requirements.
- **Incident Handling**: Act as final authority on appeals, resolve escalated issues, coordinate platform-wide announcements.

## 3. Summary Table: Access by Role

| Action/Feature                      | Member | Moderator | Admin |
|-------------------------------------|:------:|:---------:|:-----:|
| View and create posts/comments      |   ✔️    |     ✔️     |  ✔️   |
| Edit/delete own posts/comments      |   ✔️    |     ✔️     |  ✔️   |
| Report content                      |   ✔️    |     ✔️     |  ✔️   |
| Edit/delete others’ posts/comments  |        |     ✔️     |  ✔️   |
| Issue warnings/suspensions          |        |     ✔️     |  ✔️   |
| Review/act on reports               |        |     ✔️     |  ✔️   |
| Assign/revoke moderator rights      |        |           |  ✔️   |
| Configure board/system policies     |        |           |  ✔️   |

## 4. Authentication and Access Control Notes
- Role assignments are central to all API authentication and UI control logic; users only see and perform actions permitted by their current role.
- Permissions are strictly enforced to prevent unauthorized access or action escalation.

---

# Core Functional Requirements

## Overview
This document outlines the essential functional requirements for the political/economic discussion board. It covers the lifecycle of posts, permission management across roles, core features such as posting and commenting, handling of reports and moderation, and the design of notification and interaction mechanisms. Each requirement is detailed with explicit workflows, practical examples, and scenario-based clarifications for all user roles: members, moderators, and admins.

## 1. User Roles & Permissions

**Member:**
- Can create, read, comment on, and edit/delete their own posts
- Can report posts/comments violating guidelines
- Receives notifications for thread updates, moderation results, replies, etc.

**Moderator:**
- Can review and action (approve, edit, hide, or remove) reported content
- Can issue warnings, temporary bans, or mediation notes to members
- Oversees active threads for compliance; can pin/unpin posts

**Admin:**
- Full access: can manage all content and users, adjust policies, alter board configuration
- Reviews moderator actions and handles escalation cases

*Example: A member creates an economic analysis post. A moderator spots potentially misleading data and requests clarification. If unresolved, the admin may remove the post and warn the member.*

## 2. Post Creation & Management

### Requirements
- Members can draft rich-text posts with images, links, and file attachments. Each post is assigned tags (e.g., "Politics", "Economics") and can be categorized further.
- Drafts can be saved and edited before publishing. Published posts can be edited by the author (within a policy-configurable time window) or by moderators/admins (at any time).

### Workflow Example
1. Member drafts a post on recent policy changes with charts attached.
2. Before publishing, member previews and edits for clarity.
3. After submission, the post is instantly available unless flagged by automated moderation for sensitive keywords.
4. Member may later edit the post if they receive new data, as long as the edit window is open.

### Deletion
- Self-deletion: Members can delete their own posts. If the post has comments, a soft-delete hides it but retains discussion continuity.
- Moderator/admin deletion: Can permanently remove content for clear policy violations or legal reasons.

## 3. Commenting System

### Features
- Threaded comments and replies, with the ability to mention users
- Markdown support for formatting
- Comments can include attachments and links
- Moderation applies here as for posts

### Use Case
- A post on inflation generates multiple comment threads, including debates, fact-checks, and questions directed at the author. Members can "like" or "dislike" comments, and moderators watch for personal attacks, quietly resolving disputes through mediation or removal if needed.

## 4. Reporting & Moderation

### Reporting
- Any member can report a post or comment. Predefined reasons (e.g., spam, misinformation, harassment) are required; free-text evidence can be provided.
- Anonymous reporting is permitted, but abuse (e.g., repeated frivolous reports) is tracked and penalized.

### Moderation Flow
1. Moderators receive notification of new reports in a dedicated queue.
2. Each report displays full context—including history of previous moderation, user warnings, and discussion thread.
3. Moderator acts: dismisses the report, edits/soft-deletes the content, or escalates to admin.

*Scenario: A member posts unverified economic rumors. Several users report it citing guideline breaches. The moderator verifies, adds an official clarification comment, and marks the post as “Contested Information.” If repeated, the admin may temporarily suspend the user.*

## 5. Notification Mechanisms

**Triggers:**
- New replies, mentions, or moderation results
- Status change on a report you filed
- Updates to a thread you are following

**Channels:**
- On-site notifications (with dashboard aggregation)
- Optional email alerts for major actions

**Example:**
Member receives push notification: "Your post was edited by a moderator for policy compliance. View changes."

- Members can control notification preferences; certain critical notifications (e.g., warnings, suspensions) are always sent.

## 6. Search, Tagging, & Discovery

- Advanced search by keyword, tag, author, or date
- Members can follow tags or threads; discover trending discussions via an algorithmic feed
- Moderators/admins can feature timely or high-quality posts (e.g., pin to top of board)

## 7. Interaction Controls

- Likes/dislikes on posts/comments, with visible counts
- Members can bookmark threads for quick access
- Moderators/admins can disable interactions on posts (e.g., for archived or resolved threads)

## 8. Accessibility & Internationalization

- Full keyboard navigation and screen-reader support
- Multilingual UI (locale settings per member profile)
- Posts/comments must render correctly regardless of language or device

## 9. Audit & Compliance Logging

- Automatic tracking of all policy-critical actions (posting, editing, reporting, moderation decisions)
- Exportable logs for admin review or legal compliance

# 4. Non-Functional & Policy Requirements for Political/Economic Discussion Board

This section establishes the essential non-functional and policy-related requirements to operate, secure, and maintain an effective, responsible discussion environment. The aim is to ensure robust platform quality, safety, accessibility, compliance, and sustained member trust.

## 4.1 Security & Privacy
- **Authentication & Authorization**: Enforce role-based access (member, moderator, admin) for all endpoints. Validate user sessions to prevent unauthorized access.
- **Data Protection**: Use encryption (AES-256 or better) for sensitive user data at rest and TLS for data in transit.
- **PII Handling**: Store only minimal personally identifiable information. Allow users to delete or export their own data, in line with regional regulations (e.g., GDPR, CCPA wherever applicable).
- **Attack Mitigation**: Employ rate limiting, firewall rules, and WAF to prevent brute-force, DDoS, and injection attacks.
- **Audit Logging**: Log all access and moderation actions. Protect logs from tampering and restrict visibility to admins for review and compliance auditing.

## 4.2 Performance & Scalability
- **Responsiveness**: Target average API response times under 300ms for 95% of requests under normal load.
- **Throughput**: Support a minimum of 10,000 concurrent users without degradation.
- **Elastic Scaling**: Plan for cloud-auto-scaling to handle traffic peaks during political/economic events.
- **Resilience**: Ensure the board platform recovers automatically from service outages with minimal disruption.

## 4.3 Availability & Reliability
- **Uptime**: Maintain at least 99.5% uptime monthly. Announce planned maintenance with 48 hours' notice via banner.
- **Backup & Recovery**: Daily data backups and disaster recovery plans to prevent data loss. Retain backups securely for at least 90 days.
- **Service Monitoring**: Real-time monitoring of system health (CPU, memory, database, API) with automated alerting to administrators.

## 4.4 Usability & Accessibility
- **Mobile/Responsive Design**: The web interface must be fully usable across smartphones, tablets, and desktops.
- **Visual & Language Accessibility**: Adhere to WCAG 2.1 AA guidelines (alt text, keyboard navigation, ARIA labels). Support English as default, with provisions for additional languages as needed.
- **Onboarding & Help**: Provide in-product help, clear policy explanations, and user guides for new features or changes.

## 4.5 Content Moderation & Policy Compliance
- **Community Guidelines**: Clearly display posting rules and moderation policy; proactively inform users of serious updates.
- **Moderation Workflow**: Guarantee a timely response to user reports (within 24 hours). Escalate unresolved cases automatically to admins after 48 hours.
- **Automated Filtering**: Implement keyword and pattern-based detection for hate speech, defamation, spam, misinformation, and illegal content.
- **Appeals Mechanism**: Allow users to appeal moderation actions, with transparent logging and outcome notification within 7 days.
- **Legal Compliance**: Regularly review and update policies to comply with evolving regional regulations (defamation, election law, privacy, copyright).

## 4.6 Data Retention & Deletion
- **Retention Policy**: Remove posts and logs per policy (usually after 2 years) unless preservation is required for legal or compliance reasons.
- **Right to Erasure**: Enable members to request deletion of their contributions. Moderators/admins may retain minimal data for audit/legal obligations.

---

For details on functional features, refer to [03_discussionboard_core_functional_requirements.md](./03_discussionboard_core_functional_requirements.md). For system workflows and moderator processes, see [05_discussionboard_system_workflow_and_moderation_process.md](./05_discussionboard_system_workflow_and_moderation_process.md).

# 5. System Workflow and Moderation Process

## Overview
This section details the structured workflows that govern user participation and content management within the Political/Economic Discussion Board. It covers the lifecycle of posts and comments, the escalation pathway of user reports, the moderation review pipeline, and the governance processes that ensure compliance, transparency, and a healthy discourse environment.

---

## 1. Content Creation and Visibility Workflow
- **Post/Comment Submission:**
  - Any member can create or comment on public threads within the board. Upon submission, posts are immediately visible unless flagged as potentially violating content by automated filters or user reputation safeguards.
- **Immediate Display:**
  - If no red flags are detected, content is indexed and appears to all users.
- **Pre-Moderation Scenarios:**
  - Automated heuristics or new-user restrictions may temporarily restrict content pending moderator review for accounts with low trust scores or recent signup status.

---

## 2. Reporting & Escalation Mechanism
- **User-Initiated Reporting:**
  - Members can report posts or comments suspected of violating guidelines. A report dialog collects the reason (pre-defined or custom), and the target content is immediately tagged for moderator attention.
- **Automated Escalation:**
  - Posts reaching a report threshold (e.g., 5 unique reports) are automatically hidden pending review.
- **Transparency:**
  - Report status and outcomes are visible to the reporting user.

---

## 3. Moderation Review & Enforcement
- **Moderator Inbox:**
  - Flagged content appears in a prioritized queue for moderators, sorted by urgency and volume of reports.
- **Review Actions:**
  - Moderators can:
    - Approve and unhide content
    - Edit to remove sensitive details
    - Delete or permanently suppress content
    - Issue warnings or apply sanctions to violators
    - Escalate to admins for complex cases
- **Audit Trail:**
  - All actions are logged for admin oversight and potential user appeal.

---

## 4. Administrative Oversight & Policy Update
- **Admin Privileges:**
  - Admins can manage user bans, audit historical moderation records, and update community standards.
- **Periodic Review:**
  - Regular policy reviews are conducted based on incident data and community feedback.
- **Transparency Reports:**
  - Major moderation statistics (post removals, bans, etc.) are summarized via board-wide transparency reports.

---

## 5. Appeals & Restorative Workflow
- **Appeal Submission:**
  - Members may submit appeals for removed content or personal sanctions. Appeals are routed to admins.
- **Review Process:**
  - An admin reviews the case, referencing audit logs and contextual data.
- **Outcome Notification:**
  - Decisions are communicated to users with rationale; restored content, if appropriate, is re-indexed with a note for future reference.

---

## 6. Workflow Diagrams
```mermaid
graph TD;
  A[Member Posts/Comments] --> B{Automated/Manual Filter};
  B -- No Issues --> C[Visible To All];
  B -- Possible Issue --> D[Moderator Queue];
  C --> E[User Reported?];
  E -- No --> F[Remains Visible];
  E -- Yes --> D;
  D --> G{Moderation Action};
  G -- Approve/Unhide --> C;
  G -- Edit/Delete --> H[Content Modified/Removed];
  G -- Sanction User --> I[Member Warned/Sanctioned];
  H --> J[Appeal Possible];
  I --> J;
  J -- Appeal Submitted --> K[Admin Review];
  K -- Approved --> C;
  K -- Denied --> L[Action Upheld];
```

---
